figure.name: John Maynard Keynes
figure.role: Economist focused on demand, unemployment, money, crisis, and public policy inside capitalist economies.
figure.hook: Keynes = markets can stall, and policy can matter.
whyHere: Keynes belongs here because not every public intervention is socialism, and not every market economy is laissez-faire.
He matters because modern democracies often combine private markets with public spending, stabilization policy, social insurance, and regulation.
figure.cleanIdea: A mixed economy can use public policy to stabilize demand and employment without abolishing markets or private firms.

figure.discussionText: This is the planned debate room for Keynes: markets, crisis, public spending, mixed economies, unemployment, and what counts as socialism.

hallCard.timelineMeaning: Economic crisis pushes democracies toward public spending, stabilization policy, and mixed-economy arguments.

ideas.title: Mixed Economy
ideas.plainDefinition: A mixed economy combines markets, private firms, public rules, taxes, public services, and social insurance.
ideas.context: In the Keynes path, mixed economy means capitalism with public policy tools, not automatic socialism.
ideas.whyMatters: Mixed economy matters because it names the real structure many democracies use.

ideas.title: Public Spending
ideas.plainDefinition: Public spending is government spending on services, infrastructure, benefits, wages, defense, or public investment.
ideas.context: In the Keynes path, public spending can be a stabilization tool inside a market economy.
ideas.whyMatters: Public spending matters because tax-funded spending is a broad category; it is not automatically communism, socialism, or capitalism by itself.

ideas.title: Fiscal Policy
ideas.plainDefinition: Fiscal policy means using public budgets, taxes, borrowing, and spending to influence economic conditions.
ideas.context: In the Keynes path, fiscal policy is one way governments respond to unemployment and weak demand.
ideas.whyMatters: Fiscal policy matters because the argument is about public economic tools, not a simple market-versus-state slogan.
